name: Pharaoh's Cupbearer
title: The Prisoner Who Was Restored
summary: Pharaoh's cupbearer was a high-ranking official at the Egyptian court who was thrown into prison along with the baker. Joseph interpreted his dream about grape clusters, and after three days the cupbearer was restored to his position, just as Joseph had predicted. He forgot Joseph for two years but remembered him when Pharaoh needed someone to interpret dreams.

keyEvents.title: Thrown into Prison
keyEvents.description: The cupbearer fell out of favor with Pharaoh and was held in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, where Joseph also was.

keyEvents.title: The Dream About the Vine
keyEvents.description: The cupbearer dreamed of a vine with three branches that bore ripe grapes. He squeezed the grapes into Pharaoh's cup and gave it to Pharaoh.

keyEvents.title: Joseph Interprets the Dream
keyEvents.description: Joseph explained that the three branches meant three days, and that the cupbearer would be restored to his position.

keyEvents.title: Restored to Office
keyEvents.description: On Pharaoh's birthday, the cupbearer was restored to his position, just as Joseph had predicted.

keyEvents.title: Forgotten Joseph
keyEvents.description: Even though Joseph asked him to remember him before Pharaoh, the cupbearer forgot about Joseph for two full years.

keyEvents.title: Joseph Remembered by Pharaoh
keyEvents.description: When Pharaoh needed a dream interpreter, the cupbearer finally remembered Joseph and told Pharaoh about him.
